name: Section
intent: A titled block of a page, like Account information or Recent invoices: a header with a line under it, optional help and buttons, and the content below. It can collapse.
usage: Use Section to split a page under its PageHeader into titled parts, each holding a Table, FormDisplay rows, a Scoreboard or a Form. It is one component: pass title and the content as children, or leave children out for a header only, like a heading above content laid out by the page. Page edge padding and gap between Section blocks come from layout classes (`.layout-content`), not from Section — see contracts/layout.json. help adds a ? icon after the title that opens a HelpPopover. actions holds kit Buttons at the end of the header. collapsible adds a chevron button before the title that hides and shows the content; it starts expanded unless defaultExpanded is false. A Section inside another Section's children is a sub-block: its title steps down to text-heading-xs on its own, so the outer title stays the louder one. Its stacked blocks sit one grid gutter apart. line sets the rule under the header: medium (2px, the default) or thin (1px). Each Section sets its own, so a page can keep 2px lines on its sections and give their subsections thin ones. columns (1, 2 or 3) lays a Section of FormDisplay rows or kit fields out in columns, left to right: pass the rows or fields straight in as children, not wrapped in a div. Each column stops at --layout-column-max (554px) and the block stays at the start, so the space past the last column stays empty on a wide screen; the header and its line keep the full width. Columns give way as the Section narrows, like Form columns: three become two under 1301px with start labels (720px with labels on top), and two become one under 867px with start labels (560px on top). Inside a RecordPage the Section takes the record's columns and labelPosition unless it sets its own columns. A Table, Scoreboard or anything else that is not a field or a FormDisplay is never put in columns: a Section of those keeps the full width. See contracts/section.json for the full contract.

title.note: The heading, an h2. Section writes it in title case, so pass the copy either way.

description.note: One short line under the title.

help.note: Adds a ? icon after the title that opens a HelpPopover titled with the section title, like the field help icons.

actions.note: Kit Buttons or a Dropdown at the end of the header, usually size sm. One strong brand Button per view.

children.note: The section's content. Leave it out for a header only: the title row and its line, with nothing below.

line.note: The line under the header. medium is 2px, thin is 1px, both in the brand-faint color. It applies to this Section's own header only; a Section inside it sets its own.

columns.note: Lays FormDisplay rows or kit fields, passed straight in as children, out in 1, 2 or 3 columns, left to right, each at most 554px (--layout-column-max) and kept at the start. A Textarea spans the row. Unset, the Section takes the columns of the RecordPage it is in; outside one, the content stacks at full width as before. Only rows and fields go into columns: a Section of a Table or anything else stays full width.

collapsible.note: A chevron button before the title hides and shows the content.

defaultExpanded.note: Starting expanded state when collapsible and not controlled.

useWhen: Splitting a record or dashboard page into titled parts, like Account information, Contacts and Invoices.
Long detail pages where people fold away parts they don't need: make them collapsible.
Stacking titled blocks inside `.layout-content` so the page owns edge padding and between-section gap.
A quieter heading line: line thin, often on subsections under a 2px section, or on every section of a dense page.
A record's details on a wide screen: columns 2 or 3 puts the FormDisplay rows side by side instead of one long list.
doNot: Do not invent a SectionHeader, SectionTitle or a heading with a border. Use Section.
Do not override the header line with CSS or draw a border above the content. Use line.
Do not use it for the page title. Use PageHeader.
Do not use it for a list of questions that open one at a time. Use Accordion.
Do not put a Section around a Form's own sections. Form has sections.
Do not add outer padding, margin, or gap on Section for page inset or between-section rhythm. The page uses `.layout-content` (or equivalent layout class); read contracts/layout.json.
Do not invent a padded Section cousin or wrapper for spacing. Use layout classes.
Do not build a grid of FormDisplays or fields by hand, and do not stretch columns to fill a wide page. Use columns; it caps each column at 480px.
Do not use more than 3 columns, even on a 2560px or wider screen.
a11y: A section element named by its h2 title.
The chevron is a kit Button named by the title, with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the content. Collapsed content is hidden, so it is skipped by keyboard and screen readers.
The help icon is a button named About plus the title; the help text is also the heading's description.
The help icon's hit area is 24 by 24 (WCAG 2.5.8).
snippet:
<Section
  title="Account information"
  help="Details from the account record. Edit them on the account."
  collapsible
  actions={<Button size="sm" iconStart="edit">Edit</Button>}
>
  <FormDisplay label="Account name" value="Northwind Traders" />
</Section>

examples.title: Columns
examples.usage: columns puts FormDisplay rows side by side, left to right. Each column stops at 480px and the block stays at the start, so a wide page leaves the space on the right empty; the header line keeps the full width.

examples.title: Thin lines
examples.usage: line thin gives a 1px rule. Here the section keeps its 2px line and its two subsections use thin ones.
